answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through acoustic multipath profiling. Nodes verify physical separation by emitting sound pulses and measuring local reverberation. Across environments from an open ocean to a rocky canyon, an attacker must deploy dedicated acoustic transceivers per identity instead of cloning software agents. Forging a realistic echo signature is computationally intractable. However, turbulent winds distort acoustic transit times, triggering false rejections.
